raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Kimi K2.5 image benchmarks undercount input tokens because its Hugging Face processor leaves one unexpanded placeholder per image. The text-only fallback also omits chat-template tokens. Consequently, input-token totals and throughput metrics are incorrect.

For `Describe the image.` with one 224×224 image, the old count is **18**; the corrected count is **81 = 12 text + 69 vision**, matching both serving APIs.

Related: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1095

## Modifications

- Calculate image expansion using Kimi K2.5's `media_tokens_calculator` and encode formatted text directly with its tokenizer. Preserve the placeholders sent to serving.
- Add regression coverage for both APIs, text-only inputs, multiple images, non-square resolutions, and media boundary markers.
- Document the image benchmark command and token-accounting convention. Vision counts include media boundary markers.

The existing tokenizer loading path already supports Kimi K2.5. This change affects benchmark accounting only.

## Accuracy Tests

- **46 dataset tests pass**, including **14 new Kimi regression subcases**:
  `python3 test/registered/bench_fn/test_benchmark_datasets_api.py`.
- **16/16 client/server token comparisons match** using full original INT4 weights on two A2 nodes. Coverage includes text-only, single/multiple images, mixed resolutions, portrait/landscape images, and a real photograph; text + vision equals the server total throughout.
- Text, real-image, and two-image requests return complete answers (`finish_reason=stop`). Functional checks use temperature 0, max_tokens 128, and `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking": false}`.
- isort, Ruff lint/format, codespell, repository custom lint, whitespace checks, and Mintlify build/link validation pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**256/256 requests completed** across eight cases, with 32 requests and two warmups each. Random PNG images, seed 1095, text-length parameter 128, output length 16, and range ratio 1 were used. Token comparisons and benchmarks retain the default thinking template; benchmarks use the default `ignore_eos=True` (no `--disable-ignore-eos`) for fixed short outputs.

| API | Images | Concurrency | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tokens/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native | 1×224² | 1 | 739.99 | 293.65 | 3.11 |
| Native | 1×224² | 2 | 910.22 | 303.48 | 5.85 |
| Native | 2×448² | 1 | 1852.67 | 292.68 | 2.56 |
| Native | 2×448² | 2 | 2190.33 | 307.12 | 4.70 |
| OpenAI Chat | 1×224² | 1 | 694.76 | 294.36 | 3.13 |
| OpenAI Chat | 1×224² | 2 | 922.37 | 308.10 | 5.77 |
| OpenAI Chat | 2×448² | 1 | 1437.58 | 297.22 | 2.71 |
| OpenAI Chat | 2×448² | 2 | 2168.95 | 313.83 | 4.65 |

These are limited serving measurements with eager execution and concurrency ≤2. The change corrects accounting; it makes no inference-speedup claim.

<details>
<summary>Environment and reproduction</summary>

Validated on 2026-09-19 using source base `832ec39cc0324cb0e7823dc8385e27a30c356bdd`, two A2 nodes with 8×910B3 64 GiB each, CANN 9.0.0, torch/torch_npu 2.10.0, and Transformers 5.12.1. Model: ModelScope `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5`, full original INT4 weights (64 shards). Downloaded from `master`, which is not an immutable revision.

Image: `quay.io/ascend/sglang@sha256:db4f9fa26f09bd7d44cb83967ce23ce9cdf00fa41b35579bf112baef3e6955c6`.

Both nodes need the complete model and working NPU/HCCL access; containers used host networking and IPC. Inside each Ascend container, set `MODEL_PATH`, `PRIMARY_IP`, `NODE_RANK` (0/1), and the communication interface:

```bash
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME='<communication-interface>'
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="$HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME"
export HCCL_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_FORCE_CPU_IMAGE_PREPROCESSING=1
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" --trust-remote-code \
  --device npu --tp-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --dist-init-addr "$PRIMARY_IP:29795" \
  --attention-backend ascend --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn \
  --sampling-backend ascend --dtype bfloat16 \
  --context-length 2048 --chunked-prefill-size 512 \
  --max-running-requests 2 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31095
```

After startup, benchmark from a separate container shell on rank 0:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang-oai-chat --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31095 \
  --model "$MODEL_PATH" --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --dataset-name image --image-count 2 --image-resolution 448x448 \
  --image-format png --image-content random \
  --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 16 --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 2 --warmup-requests 2 --seed 1095 \
  --output-file kimi-k25-multi448-c2.jsonl
```

For the full matrix, combine backend `sglang`/`sglang-oai-chat`, images `1×224×224`/`2×448×448`, and concurrency `1`/`2`.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the contribution guide.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide functional and serving benchmark results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -192,6 +192,36 @@ python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
     --num-prompts 512
 ```
 
+### Kimi K2.5 image benchmarks
+
+Start a Kimi K2.5 server, then run the benchmark client on CPU. For Ascend A2/A3,
+follow the [Ascend installation guide](/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/getting-started/installation).
+Set `MODEL_PATH` to the checkpoint directory or Hugging Face model ID containing
+the tokenizer, processor, and configuration files.
+
+```bash Command
+MODEL_PATH=/path/to/Kimi-K2.5
+HOST=127.0.0.1
+PORT=30000
+python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
+  --backend sglang-oai-chat \
+  --host "$HOST" --port "$PORT" \
+  --model "$MODEL_PATH" --tokenizer "$MODEL_PATH" \
+  --dataset-name image \
+  --image-count 2 --image-resolution 448x448 \
+  --image-format png --image-content blank \
+  --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 32 \
+  --random-range-ratio 1 --num-prompts 16 \
+  --max-concurrency 2 --warmup-requests 2 --seed 1095 \
+  --output-file kimi-k25-images.jsonl
+```
+
+Use `--backend sglang` to exercise the native `/generate` endpoint instead.
+The client loads Kimi's custom tokenizer and accounts for the image token expansion
+using the processor's resize rules. Text-token counts include the chat template;
+vision-token counts include the expanded image tokens and surrounding media markers.
+The same accounting applies to the `mmmu` dataset.
+
 ### Choosing model and tokenizer
 
 - `--model` is required unless the backend exposes `GET /v1/models`, in which case the first model ID is auto-selected.

@@ -155,7 +155,23 @@ def create_mm_data_row(
             prompt_str = f"<image>{text_prompt}"
 
     # Calculate total tokens (text + vision)
-    if type(processor).__name__ in ("KimiK25Processor", "KimiK3Processor"):
+    if type(processor).__name__ == "KimiK25Processor":
+        # K2.5's HF processor leaves one media placeholder per image in
+        # input_ids. Serving expands each placeholder to the resized image's
+        # token count; account for that expansion without changing the prompt
+        # sent to the server or allocating pixel tensors on the benchmark client.
+        vision_tokens = sum(
+            int(
+                processor.media_processor.media_tokens_calculator(
+                    {"type": "image", "image": image}
+                )
+            )
+            for image in images
+        )
+        prompt_len = (
+            len(processor.tokenizer.encode(prompt_str)) + vision_tokens - len(images)
+        )
+    elif type(processor).__name__ == "KimiK3Processor":
         medias = [{"type": "image", "image": img} for img in images]
         prompt_len = processor(
             text=prompt_str,
@@ -191,11 +207,17 @@ def create_mm_data_row(
             add_generation_prompt=True,
             tokenize=False,
         )
-        text_prompt_len = processor(
-            text=[text_only_prompt],
-            padding=False,
-            return_tensors="pt",
-        )["input_ids"].numel()
+        if type(processor).__name__ == "KimiK25Processor":
+            # This processor requires medias, even for text-only inputs.
+            # Use its tokenizer so chat-template tokens are not lost through
+            # the raw-text fallback below.
+            text_prompt_len = len(processor.tokenizer.encode(text_only_prompt))
+        else:
+            text_prompt_len = processor(
+                text=[text_only_prompt],
+                padding=False,
+                return_tensors="pt",
+            )["input_ids"].numel()
     except Exception:
         # Fallback: just tokenize the text prompt directly
         tokenizer_to_use = (

@@ -41,6 +41,7 @@
 )
 from sglang.benchmark.datasets.image import (
     ImageDataset,
+    create_mm_data_row,
     parse_random_image_resolution,
     sample_image_requests,
 )
@@ -279,6 +280,25 @@ def __call__(self, text, medias=None, **kwargs):
         return {"input_ids": _DummyTokenTensor(text_len + 4 * len(medias))}
 
 
+class KimiK25Processor(DummyProcessor):
+    """K2.5 leaves media placeholders unexpanded in its HF input_ids."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tokenizer):
+        super().__init__(tokenizer)
+        self.media_processor = SimpleNamespace(
+            media_tokens_calculator=lambda media: {
+                (224, 224): 64,
+                (448, 448): 256,
+                (315, 513): 228,
+            }[media["image"].size]
+        )
+
+    def __call__(self, text, medias=None, **kwargs):
+        if medias is None:
+            raise ValueError("Provide both medias and text")
+        return {"input_ids": _DummyTokenTensor(len(self.tokenizer.encode(text)))}
+
+
 class _FakeMMMUDataset:
     def __init__(self, records):
         self.records = records
@@ -640,6 +660,59 @@ def test_image_sampler_uses_kimi_k3_media_contract(self):
         self.assertEqual(processor.media_call_count, 1)
         self.assertTrue(rows[0].image_data)
 
+    def test_kimi_k25_counts_expanded_images_and_chat_template(self):
+        self.tokenizer.add_special_tokens(
+            {
+                "additional_special_tokens": [
+                    "[MEDIA_BEGIN]",
+                    "[IMAGE]",
+                    "[MEDIA_END]",
+                ]
+            }
+        )
+        self.tokenizer.chat_template = (
+            "tok_2 {% for message in messages %}"
+            "{% if message['content'] is string %}{{ message['content'] }} "
+            "{% else %}{% for item in message['content'] %}"
+            "{% if item['type'] == 'text' %}{{ item['text'] }} "
+            "{% else %}[MEDIA_BEGIN] [IMAGE] [MEDIA_END] "
+            "{% endif %}{% endfor %}{% endif %}"
+            "{% endfor %}{% if add_generation_prompt %}tok_3{% endif %}"
+        )
+        processor = KimiK25Processor(self.tokenizer)
+        # Two text tokens plus the template's prefix and generation prompt.
+        text_tokens = 4
+        for backend in ("sglang", "sglang-oai-chat"):
+            # Vision counts include both boundary markers for each image.
+            for sizes, vision_tokens in (
+                ([], 0),
+                ([(224, 224)], 66),
+                ([(448, 448)], 258),
+                ([(315, 513)], 230),
+                ([(224, 224), (224, 224)], 132),
+                ([(224, 224), (448, 448)], 324),
+                ([(315, 513), (224, 224)], 296),
+            ):
+                with self.subTest(backend=backend, sizes=sizes):
+                    row = create_mm_data_row(
+                        "tok_0 tok_1",
+                        [Image.new("RGB", size) for size in sizes],
+                        ["data:image/png;base64,unused"] * len(sizes),
+                        8,
+                        processor,
+                        backend,
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(row.prompt_len, text_tokens + vision_tokens)
+                    self.assertEqual(row.text_prompt_len, text_tokens)
+                    self.assertEqual(row.vision_prompt_len, vision_tokens)
+                    if backend == "sglang":
+                        # The server, not the client, expands the sent placeholders.
+                        self.assertEqual(row.prompt.count("[IMAGE]"), len(sizes))
+                        self.assertEqual(row.prompt.count("[MEDIA_BEGIN]"), len(sizes))
+                        self.assertEqual(row.prompt.count("[MEDIA_END]"), len(sizes))
+                    else:
+                        self.assertEqual(row.prompt, "tok_0 tok_1")
+
     def test_image_sampler_random_resolution(self):
